selection_method: Sites were selected from real, already-verified repository evidence only: the 656-member Uganda CFR canonical cohort (real polygons, real August 2026 Sentinel-2 observations) and the 13-site Tanzania tree-breeding trial dataset (real field measurements, point geometry). No site or attribute was invented; two Tanzania registry entries (NFC, Tukuyu) were EXCLUDED from this manifest due to an unexplained data-quality anomaly in their measurement-age lists (see docs/eo/REPOSITORY_EO_AUDIT.md section 3) pending independent confirmation against their source Excel files.

sites.name: Kisolanza

measured_attributes: mean_dbh_cm (partially populated -- often null at young ages)

sites.why_selected: Longest clean real age series (17-91 months, ~7.6 years) with both pine and eucalyptus (species contrast) at one location -- best candidate for a real optical/SAR growth trajectory compared against real measured height/DBH trends.

sites.name: Uchindile
sites.why_selected: Richest real measurement-age series of any site (9 distinct campaigns) -- best resolution for a real growth curve, and includes corymbia as a third genus not present at Kisolanza.
sites.role_in_track_b: field-truth anchor, point-based, highest temporal resolution

sites.name: Tanwat
sites.why_selected: Southernmost clean Tanzania site (Southern Highlands) with the long 91-month series -- geographic/terrain contrast from Kisolanza and Uchindile within the same trial network.
sites.role_in_track_b: field-truth anchor, point-based, Southern Highlands terrain

sites.name: Saohill
sites.why_selected: Fourth pine-bearing site clustered near Kisolanza/Uchindile -- shorter series (to 55 months) gives a younger-stand contrast within the same broad geography.

sites.name: Tabora
sites.why_selected: Only clean site in west-central Tanzania (drier, miombo-adjacent climate) -- no pine, but the clearest available climate/geography contrast to the Southern Highlands cluster (Kisolanza/Uchindile/Tanwat/Saohill).

sites.name: Zulia
sites.why_selected: Largest CFR in the cohort (92,559 ha) with lower relative NDVI -- size and vegetation-density extreme; already used as the direct-processing-ceiling reference case, so its EO behavior is unusually well characterized.
sites.role_in_track_b: EO-geometry anchor, canonical polygon, size extreme

sites.name: Musamya
sites.why_selected: 75th-percentile area, high NDVI, near-equatorial -- a mid-large, apparently dense/productive CFR distinct from Zulia's low-NDVI extreme.
sites.role_in_track_b: EO-geometry anchor, canonical polygon, high-productivity contrast

sites.name: Epor
sites.why_selected: Median-area CFR, median-ish NDVI -- the single most 'typical' member of the 656-CFR cohort; already exercised in the EO evidence-drawer UI validation, so its full August observation (NDVI/NDMI/NBR, coverage, acquisition count) is already known end-to-end.
sites.role_in_track_b: EO-geometry anchor, canonical polygon, typical/median case

sites.name: Bunjazi
sites.why_selected: Highest NDVI of any Uganda CFR (0.845) -- the cohort's vegetation-density extreme in the opposite direction from Zulia; small enough for a fast, cheap multi-sensor pull.
sites.role_in_track_b: EO-geometry anchor, canonical polygon, high-NDVI extreme

sites.name: Kihihi
sites.why_selected: Southwesternmost clean candidate (near the Bwindi/DRC border region, materially different terrain from the other four Uganda picks) and 25th-percentile area -- smallest-scale, most geographically distinct Uganda case in the set.
sites.role_in_track_b: EO-geometry anchor, canonical polygon, geographic/terrain extreme

ug_noted_edge_case_not_selected: Mala Island (1.15 ha, NDVI -0.09 -- likely water/bare-ground dominated, not a forest-productivity extreme)

explicit_gaps: No Tanzania CFR/AOI canonical polygon geometry exists anywhere in the repository -- Tanzania sites here are point coordinates with an ASSUMED buffer, not surveyed boundaries.
No Uganda CFR has field-measured DBH/height/survival ground truth -- Uganda sites here contribute EO+geometry only.
No single site in this manifest has both a canonical polygon AND real field measurements -- that combination does not yet exist in this repository for any site.
